prompt:

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — tellurium: a brittle, lustrous silver-white metalloid found in 1782 in gold ore from the mountains of Transylvania, so puzzling it was called paradoxical gold, and named in 1798 from Latin tellus, the earth, so that its look-alike found later was named selenium, for the moon; one of the very few elements that join with gold, it formed the grey telluride ores of the 1890s gold rushes; a trace of it leaves a garlic smell on the breath; its compounds turn heat straight into electricity — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.
